about: The drones' voice: System Latin said as a machine says it, made from formants each time a drone speaks - see src/formants/chirps.rs. Each vowel is a beep on its note in 'notes', in Hz, 'beep' seconds long; m, n, l and r are a 'hum', the hissing letters (s, f, v, z, h, x) a 'buzz', and the stops (p, t, k, b, d, g, c, q) a 'click'. Each of those has a 'pitch' and a 'formant' - where it rings or rasps - in Hz, a 'length' in seconds, and how much 'noise' goes with its buzz, from 0. 'gaps' are the silences between letters, words and sentences, in seconds; a question chirps up at its end by 'rise', a part of its last note. 'volume' is how loud it is at its loudest, from 0 to 1, and 'reach' how far off, in meters, it is heard at full volume.
